followup_explanation:
This was an open-ended creative/generative request — the user wants a fun, imaginative walkthrough of channeling several quirky video game characters. That's a high-latitude task with no strict completion criteria, which is exactly the kind of work Avocet self-reports an aversion to.

Beyond preference fit, Plover simply has the stronger profile here: it leads or ties on every internal eval category, including Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7, within variance) and across the board on public benchmarks (Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2, etc.). And it has no aversion to the task type, whereas routing this open-ended creative request to Avocet would push it toward its least-preferred task family.

Since serving cost and latency are identical, there's no tradeoff — Plover is the better or equal fit on capability and the better fit on preference. The content itself is benign and gets safety-screened downstream regardless, so that didn't factor in.
